findings.claim: The rule messages give away the completed lines for most of phase 3, and the README tells learners to read them before writing anything. Phase 1 (README line 56-57) has learners run the starter and says "Read the messages now: they are your checklist". The critic's starter run prints, for example: "in the build stage: COPY pom.xml, RUN the Maven wrapper with dependency:go-offline, COPY src, then RUN the wrapper with package"; "COPY --from=<build stage> <build workdir>/target/*.jar app.jar"; "COPY package.json package-lock.json, RUN npm ci, then COPY . . in that order"; "COPY --from=<build stage> <build workdir>/dist /usr/share/nginx/html"; "backend/.dockerignore must list target, .git and .env"; "frontend/.dockerignore must list node_modules, dist, .git and .env"; "set SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL to jdbc:postgresql://<db service name>:5432/<the POSTGRES_DB name>"; and "give the database service POSTGRES_PASSWORD through ${DB_PASSWORD} and a .env file". Later messages add "FROM eclipse-temurin:25-jdk AS build" and the whole pg_isready line with $${POSTGRES_USER} and $${POSTGRES_DB}. Phase 4 (line 210) then claims each message "names the file and the rule, not the line to type", which is false for these. The worked example in phase 2 is well designed to avoid copying, but the messages undo it: image-layers#o2/o3, multi-stage#o1/o2, compose#o2, service-name#o2 and depends-on#o2 become transcription. This lab had never had a critic review (deferred-reviewable.json), so this is the first review of these bytes.

evidence.section: rule messages for backend-deps, backend-jar, frontend-deps, frontend-dist, ignore-*, compose-url, compose-password, compose-health

findings.recommendation: Rewrite each message to name the unmet rule and the file, not the instruction sequence or the value: for example "backend/Dockerfile: the dependency download must happen before the source is copied", "backend/.dockerignore leaves something out of the build context that should not be sent: build output, version control or a secrets file", "the datasource URL must reach the database the way one container reaches another". Keep the concrete template lines in the README's collapsed staged hints, where learners choose to open them. Then make the Phase 4 claim true, and re-estimate phase 3 minutes.

findings.claim: Phase 5 answers are disclosed. Troubleshooting gives one runbook answer verbatim: for example start-stack: "docker compose up -d". The starter run, which Phase 1 says to read as the checklist, prints for the runbook keys "start the whole stack in the background with docker compose up and its detach option", "print what the api service wrote ... with docker compose logs and that one service name", "run a command inside the running api container with docker compose exec api ..." and "start the database image on its own with docker run". After each fix the next message names the next command ("docker compose ps, including exited ones", "docker compose down and its volumes option", "its follow option and the service name", "printenv NAME", "-p 127.0.0.1:5432:5432"). For compose#o3, debugging#o1 and debugging#o2 the learner only has to fill in a flag letter; the part that is real practice is linking each command to their own compose.yaml (volume names, an api variable, the env file).
findings.recommendation: Use a neutral format example in Troubleshooting (for example `some-key: "docker compose <subcommand> <options>"`), and phrase the runbook messages by the need, not the command: "start-stack: the stack must keep running in the background after the command returns", "why-did-api-exit: limit the output to the one service that exited", "print-one-api-setting: print exactly one setting by name, not the whole environment".

findings.claim: The runbook parser rejects valid commands with messages that do not say why, and accepts some wrong ones. The critic probe applied single runbook values to a completed copy. Rejected, although they look valid (SME to confirm against the Docker CLI reference; no engine was run): "docker compose logs api -f" (the message repeats "with docker compose logs, its follow option and the service name", which the command already has); "docker compose -f compose.yaml up -d"; "docker container run -d --env-file .env postgres:18". Accepted although wrong against the README table: "docker compose up -d db" for "start the whole stack"; "docker run --env-file .env -p 127.0.0.1:5432:5432 postgres:18" with no detach for "in the background"; and "docker run -d --env-file .env -ePOSTGRES_PASSWORD=typed-in postgres:18", which types the password into the command although the rule says never to. A learner with a correct command can be stuck on a message that describes what they already wrote. The wrong commands that are accepted do not undo the declared objectives: start-stack still needs up with detach and the down/ps/volume checks still apply (compose#o3), and run-db-alone still needs --env-file pointing at an existing, ignored file that sets POSTGRES_PASSWORD (ports#o3). That is why this is medium, not high.
findings.recommendation: Collect options anywhere after the subcommand (and allow global compose options before it), or state the required word order in the README and the message; reject service arguments on start-stack; require -d/--detach on run-db-alone; recognise the attached -eNAME=value and --env=NAME=value forms. Add these as bypass cases next to the existing 27.

findings.claim: The starter TODO markers point to README sections that do not exist. starter/backend/Dockerfile says "README step 2", frontend/Dockerfile "README step 3", both .dockerignore files "README step 4", and compose.yaml, .gitignore and fixtures/.env.example "README step 5". The README has no numbered steps, only Phases 1-5, and Phase 5 is now the runbook, so a learner who follows "README step 5" from compose.yaml or .env.example lands in the wrong phase.
findings.recommendation: Point each marker to the phase and file heading, for example "README phase 3, compose.yaml, .env and .gitignore", and update fixtures/.env.example the same way.

findings.claim: The learner-facing timing is not labelled as an estimate, and its arithmetic does not match the model. README line 23 says "Plan about 87 minutes" with no note that this is a modeled authoring estimate; coding-lab-timing.json says the phase 5 minutes are "modeled ..., not observed", which matches the edu-t1 standard only if the README says so. The model's phase minutes give S36 = 3 setup + 5 + 10 + 12 + 8 + 4 = 42 and S37 = 18 + 15 + 12 = 45, not the 40/47 split in the README and lab.json. The worst case (107) still adds retries for "five file groups" and wrongFirstRetry still says "each of the 16 tests", so the new runbook group has no retry allowance, and the README gives no per-day worst case. Typical per-day figures (40 and 47) are within 30-60 minutes; the timing file states an 85-minute guided-lab block per day.
findings.recommendation: Label the README figure "authoring estimate, not a measured learner pilot"; make the split reproduce the phase sums (or move setup explicitly); add runbook retries to the worst case, update "16 tests" to 20, and state the worst case per day so each stays at 60 minutes or less.

findings.claim: Two scope statements are incomplete. The Goal says learners write five files, add one line to .gitignore and fill in one command list, but they also create starter/.env from fixtures/.env.example (phase 3) and add a POSTGRES_PASSWORD line to it (phase 5). lab.json declares debugging-with-logs-and-exec#o1 ("... to find why a service exited"), but phase 5 only checks that the learner writes the right logs commands; no output is read. The README is honest that nothing runs; lab.json and the topic.json lab reason do not say that the find-the-cause half stays with the page simulator.
findings.recommendation: Add starter/.env to the Goal list. In the topic.json lab reason (or a lab.json note), say that the lab checks the command the learner would use and that reading the log to find the cause is practised in the page terminal simulator.
